acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every one of the 42 capabilities has a recorded decision: matrix-authoritative, catalog-authoritative, or deliberately unseeded, and none is left undecided
evidence: 42 decisions, one per capability, in CAPABILITY_DECISIONS (scripts/ci/check-capability-matrix-agreement.mjs). THE FOURTH ANSWER IS IN THE RECORD, NOT ASSUMED AWAY: matrix_authoritative 2, catalog_authoritative 11, declared_intent_only 29, deliberately_unseeded 0. Enforced mechanically, not by review: UNDECIDED_CAPABILITY fails if a catalog capability has no decision, and STALE_DECISION_CAPABILITY fails if a decision names a capability the catalog no longer defines. Both directions are live — the test file drives each, and a 25-test run against the real chain finds 0 undecided and 0 stale.

matrix_authoritative (2, ZERO open pairs): workforce.view and workforce.manage. Both are read by RLS (12 and 43 literal policy sites plus the private.user_can_*_zone helpers), both were reconciled by DB-016 under CP-102, and the check exists to keep them at zero. The CP-094 withholding of workforce.manage from department_manager is recorded as a PAIR-level decision inside workforce.manage's reason, with the reason it is pair-level: has_perm takes no target, so a matrix grant is organization-wide by construction, and that is a property of a (role, capability) pair, not of a capability.

catalog_authoritative (11, 58 open pairs): tour.view, tour.manage, tour.delete, event.manage, routing.manage, hiring.manage, vendor.view, vendor.manage, logistics.view, logistics.manage, tour.publish. Each names why the open pairs are FALSE DENIALS rather than disclosures, an evidence citation, an owner, and a nextAction. Owner is wfc-003 for the eight that the matrix projection alone fixes; the other three carry the additional question their own shape raises (tour.publish is enforced at an RPC boundary, not row level, and is per-tour in the product).

declared_intent_only (29, 148 open pairs): every capability no RLS policy reads. EACH IS NAMED INDIVIDUALLY with a reason, an owner and a next action. There is no wildcard entry, because a wildcard is how a declared intent becomes an unexamined assumption — which is the mechanism that produced workforce.publish in the first place. A test asserts all 29 carry a reason longer than 80 characters, an owner and a next action, so a future entry cannot be a bare classification.

deliberately_unseeded: IMPLEMENTED, ENFORCED, AND APPLIED TO ZERO CAPABILITIES, and that is reported as a finding rather than papered over. The one real instance in this repository is pair-level (CP-094, above). The class is proven reachable rather than asserted to be, because a class no test can reach is a class that does not exist: FORBIDDEN_MATRIX_GRANT fires the moment a deliberately_unseeded capability gains a matrix grant, and a test drives exactly that.

NO CAPABILITY IS LEFT UNDECIDED, and the claim is falsifiable in both directions. DECISION_NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_CHAIN fails when a decision claims enforcement the chain no longer provides, and DECISION_UNDERSTATES_CHAIN fails when a new enforcement site appears and the record is stale. Both are pinned by tests; the second is pinned by INJECTING a real policy that reads workforce.publish into a copy of 20250816132000 and requiring exactly one failure naming workforce.publish.

Each decision also records the measured enforcement class it claims, and the check compares it to the chain on every run. The claim is a claim, not a restatement: if the chain grows or loses a reader the record becomes wrong and the check fails.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A CI check fails when the application capability gate and the RLS matrix disagree for any role and capability pair
evidence: scripts/ci/check-capability-matrix-agreement.mjs compares BOTH layers for ALL 504 pairs (12 roles x 42 capabilities). Layer 1 is the REAL resolveEffectiveAdminCapabilities, dynamically imported from lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts — the same module the running application imports, with the same three inputs loadCapabilities supplies and no target and no department authority, because has_perm takes no target. Layer 2 is DERIVED by replaying the chain's own 17 insert into public.org_role_permissions writes in version order across its three writers, each with its own conflict clause modelled, and the DB-016 seed parsed out of the migration that declares it. Neither layer is transcribed, so the two can actually disagree.

DEFAULT MODE exits 0 with every disagreement dispositioned; --strict exits 1 with exactly 206 STRICT_PAIR_DISAGREEMENT and no class exemption. Both are measured, not argued: exit 0 and exit 1 respectively, with the failure count asserted. The strict mode is the literal reading of the criterion and the default mode is what makes the decision record enforceable, so both readings are delivered rather than one being chosen.

BOTH DISAGREEMENT DIRECTIONS ARE COMPUTED, and the second one is a real finding rather than a formality. matrix_exceeds_gate is 0 today, and it is 0 STRUCTURALLY: resolveAdminCapabilities unions configuredPermissions — the matrix row — into the role's catalog defaults (SEC-102), so matrix(role) is a subset of gate(role) for every catalog capability. Asserted over all 504 pairs AND against the real resolver per role and per carried capability: zero counterexamples. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE MOST DECISION-RELEVANT FACT IN THIS TASK: none of the 206 is a disclosure. Every one is a caller who passes the route gate and is then denied rows — a plausible zero, which CP-098 forbids, but a NARROWER surface. That is what makes catalog_authoritative the right answer for the 11 enforced-with-open-pairs capabilities, and it is why the direction is still implemented and still fails (MATRIX_GRANT_UNMODELLED_BY_GATE): a comparator that computed only one direction would report the same 0.

THE CHECK IS NOT A NAME BLACKLIST, and this is the specific way it could have been one. Enforcement is classified by TRANSITIVE REACHABILITY from a policy predicate — a capability is enforced iff its literal is passed to has_perm inside a policy-creating statement, or inside a chain-defined function transitively reachable from one (287 chain-defined functions, 50 policy-reachable). logistics.view and logistics.manage are read ONLY through private.user_can_read_staff_zone / user_can_edit_staff_zone (20260903120000:53500, :53568) and appear in NO create policy statement anywhere, so a policy-text grep calls both unenforced. They are enforced. Measured and pinned by a test.

Nine failure rules, and the rule underneath them is stated so it cannot be quietly weakened: the check fails whenever the measured world and the recorded decisions disagree, IN EITHER DIRECTION. There is no severity level and no safe direction for a stale record, and a newly added RLS policy — a security improvement — still fails until the decision is updated.

THE CHECK IS NOT WIRED INTO CI AND THAT IS A GRANT LIMITATION, NOT AN OMISSION. package.json and .github/workflows/ci.yml are shared artefacts in a dirty 693-entry worktree and are outside this task's grant under CP-112. Handed to release in next_steps with the exact command, the exit codes, and the two legitimate ways it can go red on day one (a new capability nobody decided, or a decision the chain no longer supports). Until then the detector exists, is proven, and runs on nobody's behalf.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The check is proven able to fail before it is trusted to report clean, and its false-positive and false-negative directions are both recorded
evidence: PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL FOUR TIMES AT THE CLI, each a copy of the real 323-file chain with ONE edit, each run through the same command a pipeline would run, each with a real exit code. CAPABILITY_MATRIX_CHAIN_DIR was added specifically so the inversions are reproducible by an operator and not only inside a test. (1) Remove workforce.view from finance's matrix row in 20260926200000: exit 1, exactly 1 failure, MATRIX_AUTHORITATIVE_BREACH, 'finance/workforce.view: the decision is matrix_authoritative and zero open pairs, but the application gate grants it and the matrix does not.' (2) Make the organizations UPDATE policy read workforce.publish in 20250816132000: exit 1, exactly 1 failure, DECISION_UNDERSTATES_CHAIN, 'workforce.publish: the decision claims enforcement "none" but the chain measures "rls_policy".' (3) Make a policy read 'mystery.perm': exit 1, exactly 1 failure, UNDECIDED_MATRIX_VOCABULARY. (4) The UNMUTATED chain under --strict: exit 1, exactly 206 STRICT_PAIR_DISAGREEMENT.

DB-016's standard was 'make the comparator report 13 disagreements on the before-state'. The equivalent here is larger and is run first: --strict reports 206 on the CURRENT chain, and the default mode's 0 is only trustworthy because the same instrument reports 206 under a flag. The in-test inversions go further, to the real chain, and each asserts that its edit APPLIED before requiring the failure, so no inversion can pass vacuously.

FALSE POSITIVE — SAFE, RECORDED, AND LABELLED IN THE OUTPUT ITSELF (FALSE_POSITIVE_DIRECTION_SAFE): an unrecognised capability construct, i.e. a permission literal the chain reads that is neither a catalog capability nor a recorded legacy permission. It is reported loudly as UNDECIDED_MATRIX_VOCABULARY and an operator adds it. The check never silently ignores a construct it does not understand, and the reason is the point of AC-3: a silently ignored construct is indistinguishable from a capability that constrains nothing, which is exactly how workforce.publish came to be believed.

FALSE NEGATIVE — UNSAFE, THE DANGEROUS ONE, RECORDED, PRINTED FIRST, AND GIVEN ITS OWN SEVERITY LABEL (FALSE_NEGATIVE_DIRECTION): a RECOGNISED construct that is recorded as constraining something and no longer does. DECISION_NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_CHAIN is the rule and it is the first failure class in the output. Driven both by unit inversion and by a real-chain inversion.

THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN POST-STATE IS ASSERTED, AND ITS OWN FLOORS ARE CROSS-CHECKED, because two defects in this check's FIRST revision both produced a confident clean report from a broken instrument. (a) The statement splitter's dollar-quote branch had wrong index arithmetic, so a 'do $x$ ... $x$; create policy ...' file produced ONE statement and the second half was invisible. (b) The has_perm argument extractor was non-greedy and stopped at the first ')', so has_perm(auth.uid(), org_id, 'x') yielded the argument 'auth.uid(' — zero string literals — and 41 of the 42 capabilities were reported as constraining nothing. Both are now prevented structurally, not by care: a splitter probe and a call-argument probe run on EVERY invocation and a failed probe returns instrumentBroken and reports that the run proves nothing; and a SECOND, INDEPENDENT extractor — deliberately wrong in one specific way, hunting the closing paren with a plain depth counter that does not skip quoted strings — must find exactly the same set of 16 permission literals. A broken extractor cannot return a superset of that one. A test drives the first revision's non-greedy extractor and requires it to lose at least 10 literals, so the floor has real work to do rather than being free.

A THIRD defect was found by the test file rather than by running the check: Object.keys on a Map returns [], so the per-capability table — the table that is the whole point of the report — printed EMPTY on the first green run. A report that looked complete and omitted its own substance. Fixed in the check, not the test, and the test now asserts the presence of specific capability lines.

entries.title: CP-129 — The application capability gate is a structural superset of the RLS matrix, and the split-brain is a false-denial inventory
entries.decision: Adopt as standing knowledge: for every catalog capability, matrix(role) is a SUBSET of gate(role), because resolveAdminCapabilities unions configuredPermissions (the matrix row) into the role's catalog defaults (SEC-102). Therefore the (role, capability) split-brain is ONE-DIRECTIONAL and every open pair is a caller who passes the route gate and is then denied rows — a plausible zero, never a disclosure.
entries.reason: It was measured, not inferred: 504 pairs, zero matrix-exceeds-gate counterexamples, asserted both over the pair table and against the real resolver per role and per carried capability. The consequence is a materially different remediation priority. A gate that EXCEEDS the matrix narrows access, so the 206 pairs are a false-denial inventory, and the correct disposition for an enforced capability with open pairs is catalog_authoritative (project the matrix forward) rather than matrix_authoritative (narrow the catalog). Anyone who reads the 206 as an exposure list will prioritise it wrongly, and DB-016's own record framed it as a split-brain without stating the direction.
entries.consequences: Widening org_role_permissions is a false-denial fix, so it is a product-priority decision about who is being refused authority, not a security-urgency decision. AND it carries DB-016's named cost: capability_version digests perms IN ORDER, so ANY mutation invalidates every active acting-context session for every role touched. All roles must land in one migration and re-activation verification is a PREFLIGHT step.

entries.title: CP-130 — A capability that no RLS policy reads is a declared intent, and a matrix value for it is inert
entries.decision: Adopt a fourth disposition alongside matrix-authoritative, catalog-authoritative and deliberately-unseeded: declared_intent_only. A capability whose literal is passed to no enforcement site in the active chain constrains no row-level access, and any value for it in org_role_permissions is INERT — it reads as authority in a table dump and grants nothing. Such a capability must be labelled as declared intent and must never be counted as enforced.
entries.reason: 29 of the 42 capabilities in this repository are in this class, so a three-way classification silently forces them into one of the other three buckets, and each of those buckets carries an enforcement claim that is false. workforce.publish is the instance the class was written for: DB-016 seeded it into eight roles so the matrix would agree with the route gate, it is read by no policy, function or trigger anywhere in the 323-migration chain, and its only occurrence is a CHECK constraint that admits the value and authorizes nothing. finance.manage is a second, previously unrecorded instance: in the catalog, in the matrix for three roles since 20250816132000, and read by nothing. With finance.view, finance.approve, finance.pay and advance.manage also unread, the chain enforces no finance capability at the row level, which is a launch-relevant fact that a per-family reading would have hidden.
entries.consequences: The class is not a label, it is a rule with teeth: a decision whose measured enforcement is weaker than it claims fails the check as the FALSE-NEGATIVE direction, and a new reader of a declared-intent capability fails it too, because a check that rewards being stale is not a check. A consequence nobody should be surprised by: because the matrix is a superset of what RLS reads, the 9 inert matrix grants are an acceptable steady state and removing them is a REMOVAL, which DB-016's additivity rule forbids. The correct action is to label them, and to route the underlying question to the capability's owner.

entries.title: CP-131 — Enforcement must be classified by transitive reachability from a policy predicate, not by a grep of policy text
entries.decision: Adopt as the method for classifying whether a capability is RLS-enforced: a capability is enforced if and only if its literal is passed to the matrix authority inside a statement that creates a policy, or inside a chain-defined function transitively reachable from such a policy. A statement that merely NAMES a permission in prose, or a literal that appears only in an RPC guard, a trigger or a CHECK constraint, is not row-level enforcement and must be classified as such.
entries.reason: The grep answer is wrong in the dangerous direction and the repository contains the proof. logistics.view and logistics.manage are read only through private.user_can_read_staff_zone / user_can_edit_staff_zone (20260903120000:53500, :53568) and appear in NO create policy statement anywhere, so a policy-text grep reports both as constraining nothing. They are enforced. The converse also exists: tour.publish is enforced by three publication RPCs that call has_perm and then RAISE, and no policy reads it at all, so a policy-only instrument reports it as unenforced on a launch-critical publication path. event.manage shows the third shape, 14 of its 60 policy sites built dynamically inside execute $p$ ... $p$ DO blocks, which a splitter that mishandles dollar-quotes loses entirely.
entries.consequences: Any RLS classification tool in this repository needs a call graph, not a text matcher, and needs a statement splitter that is correct on dollar-quoted bodies. Both of this task's own first-revision defects were in that machinery and both produced a confident clean report: a splitter that lost the second half of a file, and an argument extractor that found 41 of 42 capabilities constraining nothing. The standing rule generalises — assert your own post-state, and check that the instrument can fail before believing that it did not. Note the count of policy sites is also not a count of policies: a capability read by 46 literal and 14 dynamic sites is one capability with one enforcement class, and conflating the two is how a single reader gets reported as sixty controls.

entries.title: CP-132 — The 42-capability pair table is not the whole authorization story, and the vocabulary gap is not a missing control
entries.decision: Adopt as standing knowledge: the application catalog and the RLS matrix do not share a vocabulary. Nine permissions in org_role_permissions are not capabilities, and THREE of them are read by RLS — org.manage, org.invite and staff.manage. Conversely org.roles.manage, org.settings.manage and communications.send are capabilities with no matrix row at all, while the chain enforces authority for the first two as org.manage and for the third as staff.manage.
entries.reason: It changes the remediation from 'find the missing control' to 'map the names', and getting that backwards sends people to build controls that already exist. The measurement is 16 distinct permission literals read through the chain's single matrix authority public.has_perm, against a 42-item catalog, with a 9-item legacy remainder — and the only policy that touches the matrix directly is roleperms_select ... using (true), which is world-readable and authorizes nothing. A 42x12 pair count cannot surface a control the catalog cannot name, so any inventory built from pairs is structurally blind to it.
entries.consequences: Any future capability-count-based security claim must state the vocabulary remainder alongside the pair count or it is incomplete by construction. org.roles.manage and org.settings.manage are vocabulary gaps, not missing controls, and communications.send and site_map.* are the same shape against staff.manage and the logistics vocabulary. A tenth unrecognised literal now fails scripts/ci/check-capability-matrix-agreement.mjs, so the remainder cannot grow silently.
